A new test reads a home\\u0027s coanda.db whole straight after disposing a daemon on that home and passes on both CI legs, and the pull request says whether that test failed on the Windows leg before the fix.\u0022,\u0022After the fix, RecordExportTests passes 100 consecutive runs of the class and 10 consecutive runs of the full suite on this Mac, and the pull request gives the commands and the results.\u0022,\u0022No test is skipped, retried, wrapped in a retry loop, or given a longer wait; no existing assertion changes; and no new call to the process-wide SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools is added.\u0022,\u0022dotnet build --configuration Release succeeds with warnings as errors, and dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build passes on both CI legs.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Why\\n\\nA verification run on this Mac of a change that touches no export code failed one test of 2,114: RecordExportTests.A_rebuild_refuses_when_the_records_last_event_is_not_the_one_the_export_names_and_changes_nothing, with System.IO.IOException \\u0027The process cannot access the file .../coanda-tests/\\u003Cid\\u003E/coanda.db because it is being used by another process\\u0027, thrown from SafeFileHandle.Open. The same message appeared earlier on the Windows CI leg in RecordExportTests (PR #69, main after #71). PR #74 (bc8dce2c) hardened daemon.json but did not reach the coanda.db case. It happens on macOS, so it can be diagnosed locally.\\n\\n## What the code shows at 2bdefd1\\n\\n- Nothing opens coanda.db with FileShare.None. The only .NET FileStream opens of it are \\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/NodeHome.cs:203\\u0060 (FileShare.ReadWrite, only when the file is first created) and the test\\u0027s whole-file read, \\u0060File.ReadAllBytes\\u0060 in \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060 at \\u0060tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/RecordHomes.cs:224\\u0060. Not every open goes through \\u0060OwnerOnly.Open\\u0060; that read does not.\\n- The other side is most likely a SQLite connection. The daemon\\u0027s store connects with \\u0060Data Source={databasePath}\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Store/StoreConfiguration.cs:32\\u0060), so Microsoft.Data.Sqlite pools its connections process-wide. \\u0060RunningDaemon.DisposeAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonHost.cs:354\\u0060) disposes the host and then releases the home lock; nothing closes the pooled connections, so they stay open on the home\\u0027s coanda.db after the daemon is gone.\\n- On macOS, flock and fcntl locks on the same file do conflict, even within one process: a fcntl write lock on a byte range, which SQLite takes, refuses the shared flock with LOCK_NB that .NET takes for a read. This was checked on this Mac with a two-descriptor probe. On Linux the two kinds are independent. On Windows a FileShare.Read open is refused whenever SQLite holds the file open for writing, idle or not.\\n- \\u0060SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools()\\u0060 runs in \\u0060RecordExport.cs:81\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs:63\\u0060 and \\u0060:97\\u0060, \\u0060RecordHomes.cs:115\\u0060, and \\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:260\\u0060. It closes every idle pooled connection in the test process, including a disposed daemon\\u0027s on another test\\u0027s home. Closing the last connection to a record in write-ahead-log mode checkpoints it and takes an exclusive lock on coanda.db, which is when a concurrent whole-file read is refused. Pool pruning can close them too.\\n- In RecordExportTests, the failing test (\\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:425\\u0060) is the only one that reads a home\\u0027s files whole (\\u0060:436\\u0060, \\u0060:440\\u0060) after an in-process daemon ran on that same home (\\u0060:431\\u0060).\\n\\nRead \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060, \\u0060RunningDaemon\\u0060, \\u0060StoreConfiguration.Configure\\u0060, and the failing test first. \\u0060RecordExport.cs\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs\\u0060, \\u0060HomeLock.cs\\u0060, and \\u0060OwnerOnly.cs\\u0060 explain the lock and the existing pool handling.\\n\\n## Direction\\n\\nThe smallest fix that ends the problem is for \\u0060RunningDaemon\\u0060 to close the connections in its own pool, for its own connection string and not process-wide, before it releases the home lock. That keeps \\u0060HomeLock\\u0060\\u0027s promise that an export or rebuild never runs beside a daemon, and it covers every test that inspects a home after a daemon, not only this one. A fix confined to the test would leave the next such test with the same race.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\nNo change to the export file format, the rebuild\\u0027s behaviour, or the record\\u0027s schema. The existing \\u0060ClearAllPools\\u0060 calls stay as they are. The pull request gives the commands and the results.\u0022,\u0022No test is skipped, retried, wrapped in a retry loop, or given a longer wait; no existing assertion changes; and no new call to the process-wide SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools is added.\u0022,\u0022dotnet build --configuration Release succeeds with warnings as errors, and dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build passes on both CI legs.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Why\\n\\nA verification run on this Mac of a change that touches no export code failed one test of 2,114: RecordExportTests.A_rebuild_refuses_when_the_records_last_event_is_not_the_one_the_export_names_and_changes_nothing, with System.IO.IOException \\u0027The process cannot access the file .../coanda-tests/\\u003Cid\\u003E/coanda.db because it is being used by another process\\u0027, thrown from SafeFileHandle.Open. The same message appeared earlier on the Windows CI leg in RecordExportTests (PR #69, main after #71). PR #74 (bc8dce2c) hardened daemon.json but did not reach the coanda.db case. It happens on macOS, so it can be diagnosed locally.\\n\\n## What the code shows at 2bdefd1\\n\\n- Nothing opens coanda.db with FileShare.None. The only .NET FileStream opens of it are \\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/NodeHome.cs:203\\u0060 (FileShare.ReadWrite, only when the file is first created) and the test\\u0027s whole-file read, \\u0060File.ReadAllBytes\\u0060 in \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060 at \\u0060tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/RecordHomes.cs:224\\u0060. Not every open goes through \\u0060OwnerOnly.Open\\u0060; that read does not.\\n- The daemon\\u0027s store connects with \\u0060Data Source={databasePath}\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Store/StoreConfiguration.cs:32\\u0060), so Microsoft.Data.Sqlite pools its connections. The pool does not outlive the daemon, though: Fisher 1.27.0 registers its \\u0060DocumentStore\\u0060 through a factory, so the host\\u0027s container disposes it, and \\u0060FisherDatabase.DisposeAsync\\u0060 then calls \\u0060SqliteConnection.ClearPool\\u0060 for its own connection string. When \\u0060RunningDaemon.DisposeAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonHost.cs:354\\u0060) returns, the daemon\\u0027s idle pooled connections to that home\\u0027s coanda.db are already closed. A connection checked out at that moment is closed only when its holder releases it, and a native SQLite handle whose close is deferred by an unfinalized statement stays open until the statement is finalized. Either would close later and checkpoint the write-ahead log under an exclusive lock. Neither has been shown to happen.\\n- On macOS, flock and fcntl locks on the same file do conflict, even within one process: a fcntl write lock on SQLite\\u0027s shared byte range refuses the shared flock with LOCK_NB that .NET takes for a read, while a fcntl read lock on the same range does not. This was checked on this Mac with a two-descriptor probe. On Linux the two kinds are independent. On Windows a FileShare.Read open is refused whenever SQLite holds the file open for writing.\\n- \\u0060SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools()\\u0060 runs in \\u0060RecordExport.cs:81\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs:63\\u0060 and \\u0060:97\\u0060, \\u0060RecordHomes.cs:115\\u0060, and \\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:260\\u0060, and closes every idle pooled connection in the test process; whether it plays any part here is unproven.\\n- The home\\u0027s lock is released by the \\u0060ApplicationStopped\\u0060 callback at \\u0060DaemonHost.cs:290-301\\u0060 when a daemon stops, before the host and its store are disposed; every daemon in RecordExportTests is stopped before it is disposed.\\n- In RecordExportTests, the failing test (\\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:425\\u0060) is the only one that reads a home\\u0027s files whole (\\u0060:436\\u0060, \\u0060:440\\u0060) after an in-process daemon ran on that same home (\\u0060:431\\u0060). The rebuild between those reads opens coanda.db only through \\u0060RecordExport.ConnectUnchanged\\u0060, which uses \\u0060Pooling = false\\u0060 (\\u0060RecordExport.cs:209-217\\u0060).\\n\\nRead \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060, \\u0060RunningDaemon\\u0060, \\u0060StoreConfiguration.Configure\\u0060, and the failing test first. \\u0060RecordExport.cs\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs\\u0060, \\u0060HomeLock.cs\\u0060, and \\u0060OwnerOnly.cs\\u0060 explain the lock and the existing pool handling. Fisher\\u0027s disposal path is in \\u0060FisherDatabase.DisposeAsync\\u0060 and \\u0060ReleasePooledConnections\\u0060 in the Fisher 1.27.0 package.\\n\\n## Direction\\n\\nDiagnose before fixing. The failure has one observed occurrence on macOS and some on the Windows leg, and the daemon\\u0027s own idle connections are already closed on dispose, so the pair is not yet known. Find the open that still holds coanda.db when the whole-file read runs, prove it with a handle listing or a test that builds the pair, and fix it as close as possible to where that connection or handle is opened, without a process-wide pool clear.
